THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER Heard the learned counsel for the parties.
2. The petitioners are sought to be prosecuted for the offences punishable 306, 498A r/w 34 of IPC which is impugned in which petition.

3. Petitioners accused Nos.2 and 3 are the parents of the deceased 1st wife of accused No.1, accused No.1 is the husband of the deceased, and the deceased committed suicide by setting herself ablaze after drowning herself with petrol, and the husband immediately took her to the hospital but succumbed to the burn injuries sustained by her.
It is stated that before the death, the dying declaration was given by the deceased in the ICU of the Victoria Hospital.
In the said dying declaration she has specifically stated that, unable to bear the harassment meted by the accused No.1 she has taken extreme step of committing suicide.

4. The specific allegation against the accused Nos.2 and 3 is that, accused Nos.2 and 3 are the parents of the deceased 1st wife of the accused No.1 and they used to cooperate with the accused No.1 in harassing the deceased.

It is further alleged that they used to visit the matrimonial home frequently to see their grandchild who was born from the NC: 2023:KHC:40986 wedlock of accused No.1 and their deceased daughter i.e. 1st wife of the accused No.1.
5.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in catena of decisions has held that, to constitute the commission of offence punishable under Section 306 of IPC, the following essential ingredients must be satisfied:
i) There must be an intention on the part of the accused to aid or instigate or abet the deceased to commit suicide.
Dr.Thayalan S vs State Of Karnataka on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29003700/
2 ii) There must be a suicidal death and abetment thereof.
iii) There must a continuous harassment meted out by the accused before the death.
iv) Such irritation or annoying must be proximate to the time of occurrence of death.
6.

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Gurcharan Singh (supra) has held that in order to convict a person under Section 306 IPC, there has to be a clear mens rea to commit an offence and that there ought to be an active or direct act leading the deceased to commit suicide, being left with no option.

7. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Geo Varghese (supra) at para 23 has held as follows:
"23. What is required to constitute an alleged abetment of suicide under Section 306 IPC is there must be an allegation of either direct or indirect act of incitement to the commission of NC: 2023:KHC:40986 offence of suicide and mere allegations of harassment of the deceased by another person would not be sufficient in itself,
unless, there are allegations of such actions on the part of the accused which compelled the commission of suicide.

Further if the person committing suicide is hypersensitive and the allegations attributed to the accused is otherwise not ordinarily expected to induce a similarly situated persons to take the extreme step of committing suicide, it would be unsafe to hold the accused guilty of abetment of suicide.

Thus, what is required is an examination of every case on its own facts and circumstances and keeping in consideration the surrounding circumstances as well,
which may have bearing on the alleged action of the accused and the psyche of the deceased."
8.

In the instant case, the allegation is that the accused herein used to frequently visit the matrimonial home to see their grandchild who was born from the wedlock of accused No.1 and their deceased daughter i.e, the 1st wife of the accused No.1.
Except omnibus and general allegations against the petitioners herein there is no specific allegation as to how and in what manner they used to subject the deceased to cruelty.

Therefore, in the absence of any specific overt acts, petitioners who are the parents of the deceased 1st wife of the accused No.1 cannot be prosecuted for the offence under Section 498A of IPC.
9.

There is no allegation that the petitioners-accused Nos.2 and 3 incited or abetted the deceased to commit suicide, except stating that the petitioners herein joined with accused No.1 to harrass the deceased.

Besides, it is not the case of the NC: 2023:KHC:40986 prosecution that the accused herein possessed the knowledge or intention with their acts lead to the deceased committing suicide and without knowledge or intention, there can be no abatement.

There is no proximity to the harassment meted out by the petitioner and the date of incident, since admittedly the petitioners were not residing in the matrimonial home nor were present as on the date of the incident or prior to date of incident.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i) The Criminal Petition is allowed.
ii) The impugned proceedings in C.C.No.13925/2022 pending on the file of V Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru insofar it relates to Petitioners is hereby quashed.
iii) The learned Magistrate to proceed against accused No.1 in accordance with law,
without being influenced by any of the observations made in this order, and the observation made, if any, is only for the purpose of the present petition.
Sd/-
